raw_record.question_text: Please choose the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows. <image_1>

method.method_draft: First ignore the reaction arrows as instructed. From the image, transcribe the left reagent as methylamine: the line ending attached to NH2 represents CH3-NH2, giving SMILES CN. Then transcribe the carbonyl compound: the top carbonyl is an aldehyde carbon bearing H, attached through two methylene vertices to a terminal CHO group, giving OHC-CH2-CH2-CHO, SMILES O=CCCC=O. Combine the disconnected components with a dot to obtain CN.O=CCCC=O.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中左上方有一个“—NH2:”基团，氮前面的短线表示连接到一个甲基；图中还画有一条含两个醛基的碳链，上端是带有H的醛羰基，底端标注为CHO。图中存在弯曲箭头，但题目要求忽略箭头。
推理：忽略箭头后，左侧试剂为甲胺，SMILES为CN。右侧羰基化合物为OHC-CH2-CH2-CHO，即丁二醛，SMILES可写作O=CCCC=O。两个组分未成键，因此用点号连接，得到CN.O=CCCC=O。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct image-to-SMILES transcription: identify each disconnected molecular component in the transition-state drawing and encode them separately. This is the natural single route because the task asks only to ignore arrows and name the depicted structure.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the drawing as two disconnected species, ignoring all curved arrows: a methylamine fragment shown as a terminal line attached to NH2 with a lone pair, and a four-carbon chain bearing aldehyde groups at both ends. The upper/right end is an aldehyde carbonyl with H on the carbon and O double-bonded; the lower/right label is CHO, giving the second aldehyde terminus.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that the answer should be a SMILES expression for the shown transition-state structure while ignoring arrows; no other textual chemical data are needed.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use skeletal-structure conventions: an unlabeled line end before NH2 is a carbon with hydrogens, so it is CH3NH2, encoded as CN. A terminal carbonyl carbon bearing H is an aldehyde; the chain OHC-CH2-CH2-CHO is succinaldehyde/butanedial, encoded as O=CCCC=O. Disconnected molecules in SMILES are separated by a dot.
